articles.title: Jay-Z to headline 2027 Super Bowl half-time show
articles.summary: The man who has helped produce the Super Bowl show for years is stepping up to perform himself, at SoFi Stadium in California. After years of producing the Super Bowl half-time show, Jay-Z has announced that the 2027 headline act will be none other than himself.
body: After days of speculation, the NFL, Apple Music and Jay-Z’s company Roc Nation announced on Monday night that the rapper will be the featured performer for the half-time festivities at the Super Bowl LXI on 14 February at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” said the 56-year-old rapper in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league’s entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl half-time show, beginning with Shakira and Jennifer Lopez’s performance at Super Bowl LIV in 2020.
At the time, Jay-Z said he had told NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, “If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now.”

articles.title: Harry Kane claims men’s Ballon d’Or to end England’s 25-year wait for winner
articles.summary: Alexia Putellas picks up women’s award for third time. England captain acclaimed in London ceremony. Harry Kane is the Ballon d’Or winner for 2026, the first Englishman to win football’s most prestigious individual trophy in 25 years.
body: Two hours into a lavishly excitable ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London, Kane’s name emerged from the final envelope to wild cheers inside the auditorium. The women’s Ballon d’Or, awarded moments earlier, was won by Alexia Putellas of London City Lionesses, a third Ballon, five years on from her first in the colours of Barcelona.

In the men’s voting, Kane finished ahead of co-favourites Lamine Yamal of Barcelona and Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid, an outcome that will perhaps cause the familiar consternation among the hierarchy of those clubs, not to mention the vast online fan army attached to the superstar players in Kane’s wake.

But Kane is also a fully deserving winner of football’s ultimate gong. The L’Équipe-sponsored trophy is awarded by a vote of journalists and administrators across the footballing super-scape. For Kane, it is reward for a year during which he has won the European Golden Boot, played a major role in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga title, captained England to a World Cup semi-final, and above all shown himself to be a wonderfully humble superstar player.

Harry Kane is the Ballon d’Or winner for 2026, the first Englishman to win football’s most prestigious individual trophy in 25 years.

articles.title: Fighters exploited & forgotten in failing system - Smith
articles.summary: Fighters are being "hurt, exploited or forgotten" in a failing system, says former boxer Paul Smith, who has criticised a lack of support for athletes.
body: Smith is part of a team set up to represent fighters and safeguard their futures, with the group aiming to launch the "biggest ever inquiry into health and safety in combat sport".
The group, called the Global Fighters' Association (GFA), wants the inquiry to provide the platform for it to become "the new umbrella organisation for all combat sport".
It was set up last year with the aim of creating a union to safeguard fighters' futures.
The GFA says it wants to campaign for fair contracts and better pay, insurance and pensions, proper health and safety standards and somewhere for fighters to report problems to an official channel.

articles.title: Kane prematurely announced as Ballon d'Or winner - but he wasn't only one
articles.summary: Harry Kane's dream of winning the Ballon d'Or came true on Monday, but a few hours earlier organisers prematurely released an article claiming he had clinched the award.
body: Harry Kane was crowned winner of the men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night, but a few hours earlier that confirmation appeared to have been announced prematurely.
At 17:15 GMT, an article from the award's official website titled 'Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or' began to circulate online.

The widespread sharing of the article caused confusion online, with some wondering whether France Football - the organisers of the award - had fallen short at the final hurdle of keeping the winner, who was voted for by journalists at the end of September, under wraps.

That was until further digging on the Ballon d'Or website revealed that some of the other favourites to win the award - including Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe - also had similar pieces penned and published about them.

articles.title: From forgettable EFL loans to Ballon d'Or winner - Kane's 'Cinderella story'
articles.summary: From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale.
body: "This is a Cinderella story we've never seen before," ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his full Premier League debut, tells Sky Sports.
"He keeps breaking records, and I keep thinking, 'Are we talking about the same kid?'
"There was always a chance, because he felt like there was no ceiling - he would always just break through and go further.
"I mean, not even Harry would say he could believe it, I would suggest."

articles.title: Thunder's Williams requires surgery for broken leg and dislocated ankle
articles.summary: Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams will need surgery to repair a broken left fibula and dislocated left ankle after being stretchered off during their 108-101 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.
body: Williams - a shooting guard who entered Sunday having averaged 18 points per game in his first 250 NBA contests - has been an All-Star and an All-NBA player already in his career and was a huge part of the Thunder team that won the 2024-25 NBA title.

He injured his lower left leg and saw his ankle turn at an unnatural angle in a drive with 1:14 remaining, with Williams immediately treated by medical personnel after going down underneath the basket on the Thunder's offensive end.
"Dub, as everybody knows, is as tough as they come," Thunder GM Sam Presti said at a news conference in Oklahoma City.
"He's an elite competitor. Even last night, just miraculous in terms of his outlook and the way he's looking forward to attacking this. We're going to be with him the entire way."

articles.title: Hearts chairman calls for greater transparency on key decisions
articles.summary: Reflecting on last season's final-day title disappointment, Hearts chairman Calum Paterson calls for "greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football".
body: Talking to club media to mark his first year in the post, Paterson spoke with pride about coming so close to a first title in 66 years, but also voiced frustration around how last season's thrilling climax unfolded.
The Edinburgh side topped the Premiership table for 250 days but finished two points behind Celtic after a dramatic final-day defeat in Glasgow.

Lawrence Shankland struck first for the visitors, only for the reigning champions to find two late goals for a 3-1 victory, sparking a pitch invasion from jubilant home fans and a hasty exit for the beaten challengers, who expressed safety fears.

"The final week was difficult on a number of fronts," said Paterson. "Among other things we were disappointed by the unprecedented decision that as the team leading the league at the time of the split had to play our final game away from home.

articles.title: Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend
articles.summary: Harry Kane becomes the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London.
body: The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others.
Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom.
Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three.
"Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane told Dazn.

articles.title: WNBA’s Record Growth Raises Questions About Finals Game 6 Timing
articles.summary: The WNBA faces criticism over its 12:30 p.m. Finals Game 6 tipoff as record attendance and viewership raise questions about how women’s sports are valued.
body: The WNBA has spent the past several seasons demonstrating its ability to attract massive audiences, sell out arenas, and command national attention. Yet, with a potential WNBA Finals Game 6 scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena, the league faces questions about whether its championship is being positioned to maximize that momentum.

The demand for women’s basketball is evident. The first two WNBA Finals games played at State Farm Arena sold out, drawing approximately 17,000 fans each. According to ESPN’s Alexa Philippou, 10,000 tickets for Game 6 sold within the first two hours after going on sale.
The Golden State Valkyries have also sold out more than 51 regular-season and playoff games since entering the league in 2025, demonstrating the appetite for women’s basketball in new markets.

articles.title: Brewers fans' lucky superstitions just may be fueling the postseason
articles.summary: There may be more behind the magic of the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers ' historic postseason run than what's happening on the field. Behind every home run, double play and strikeout, the superstitions of the fans in the stands may be helping to fuel the team's nail-biter wins.
body: Dale Grudnowski — the resident cook of his tailgate group — may don a Brewers chef's hat while manning the grill at his pre-game cookout, but he wears his biggest superstition on his feet.
"These socks I have on now, I wore them for Game 1 and Game 2," he said.
Grudnowski smiled and nodded his head up and down, but he eventually relented to the truth. "No..." he winced with a smile.
Melissa Richter has been a Brewers fan since the early 1980s, and she's held on to a memento for almost as long as it took for the Brewers to return to the Fall Classic.

articles.title: Man Utd players set to return to training with Carrick's future still uncertain
articles.summary: Manchester United's players are set to return to training at Carrington on Tuesday - but it is still uncertain whether Michael Carrick will be in charge.
body: United head coach Carrick was at Carrington on Monday to watch the club's U21s take on Hull in a behind-closed-doors game.

The first-team players had a scheduled day off but Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, director of football, also met at the training base, with their talks focused on next steps following Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.
It remains to be seen what the United hierarchy, which includes Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the part-owner, will decide.

United's defeat to Bournemouth saw Carrick drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench after he questioned his tactics following the 4-1 Champions League loss to Como. It extended United's winless run to eight games across all competitions.

articles.title: Rays’ Chandler Simpson makes up for base running faux pas with epic World Series catch
articles.summary: Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Down 2-0, the Tampa Bay Rays desperately need to take Game 3 of the World Series. Outfielder Chandler Simpson is doing his part after making an incredible catch at the wall in the second inning.
body: Rays' Chandler Simpson makes up for base running faux pas with epic World Series catch appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Rays outfielder Sal Frelick thought he had an extra base hit after he took a Freddy Peralta fastball to the opposite field. However, Simpson had other ideas as he came flying out and leapt full-speed to make the catch before crashing hard into the wall.
A different angle of the play shows just how forceful Simpson's impact on the wall was, making his play all the more impressive.

Simpson's sensational catch helped make up for his base-running error earlier in the game. After getting on base via a fielder's choice in the first inning, Simpson attempted to seal second on Brewers pitcher Robert Gasser. However, the Rays outfielder missed second base with his slide and was easily tagged out to end the inning.
